items.title: Doc Cheatham interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, New York City, New York, July 28, 1995
items.q: I was with Albert Wynn’s Creole Jazz Band when we made that recording.

ctx.x: Oh, yes. I was with Albert Wynn’s Creole Jazz Band when we made that recording. I knew Ma Rainey because I sat in the Bijou Theater playing shows with the pit band. I wasn’t getting paid, I did it because they let me do it. And I just did it to try to learn as much as I could. And Ma Rainey, she came, she was the ugliest blues singer on earth when she got old, but when she was young she was pretty. You see her picture, she was the prettiest, nice looking girl. But she is so ugly, that that’s what they call the…

items.title: 54270_Doc Cheatham oral history interview
items.q: I did a lot of solo work with him.

ctx.x: Course, as I said, I wouldn't call that jazz. I didn't get into to solo jazz playing, I don't think, until let's see. Well Albert Wynn that was when -- I did -- as a saxophone player. I did a lot of solo work with him. And

Jelly Roll Jelly Roll with Teddy Rowe, Teddy Rowe was a great admirer -- he admired me quite a lot but he never got a chance to use me much. He taught me also a lot about solo playing, about half cocking the mute in the bell, now he was the originator of that. He taught me that.
